F1.title: End-to-end USV-to-decision pipeline
F1.caption: Signature figure: the full pipeline from the recording rig through segmentation and CNN syllable typing to the two preprocessing representations (tabular and sequence), the model families, the evaluation protocol, and interpretation.

F2.title: Data provenance & single source of truth
F2.caption: From scattered, undocumented inputs to a curated canonical dataset (single source of truth) with a versioned manifest and a reproducible pipeline; the genotype data-integrity correction is applied at the canonical-file stage.

F3.title: Experimental-design matrix
F3.caption: Which model/representation was evaluated under which split and cohort scope; cells show test accuracy (— = not run). Tabular models are evaluated at recording level, sequence models at session level.

F4.title: Model taxonomy — inherited vs new
F4.caption: Model families tried, by representation. Only the single subject-dependent XGBoost existed at handoff; the tuned XGBoost, TabPFN, and all three sequence models were added by this project.

F4b.title: Reported-vs-corrected baseline
F4b.caption: The previously reported subject-dependent accuracy (0.829) is not reproduced by the corrected, leak-free pipeline. Two separable effects: (i) data-integrity correction within the subject-dependent regime (0.829→0.733), and (ii) honest generalization under the subject-independent split (0.733→0.693 for XGBoost; the best honest model, TabPFN, reaches 0.729).

F5.title: Dataset composition (small multiples)
F5.caption: Counts of mice and syllables across genotype, year, strain, sex, and postnatal day for the raw corpus. The cohort is WT-skewed (~3:1) and longitudinal (P4/P6 dominate).

F6.title: Class balance and syllables-per-subject
F6.caption: Left: recording-level class balance (9,283 WT / 3,040 HT, ~3:1). Right: per-mouse syllable counts (median 828), showing the strongly longitudinal structure that motivates subject-grouped evaluation.

F7.title: Syllable-type distribution
F7.caption: Distribution of the 10 confidently-typed classes plus the post-hoc low-confidence 'Undefined' class, coloured by complexity group. 'Frequency steps' dominates; 'Undefined' (~10%) is dropped in the tabular track but retained in the sequence track.

F8.title: Acoustic-feature distributions by genotype
F8.caption: Per-syllable start/end frequency, duration and inter-syllable interval for WT vs HT (outliers hidden, display-clipped). These are the spectral/temporal features Shekel et al. (2021) reported as most ASD-sensitive.

F9.title: Master performance — dependent vs independent
F9.caption: Headline comparison of the three tabular models on the pooled baseline. Each dumbbell links the optimistic subject-dependent score (light) to the honest subject-independent score (dark). TabPFN is best on both; the dependent→independent drop is the cost of generalizing to unseen mice.

F10.title: Generalization gap (HT recall & precision)
F10.caption: Slope chart of HT recall and HT precision as evaluation moves from subject-dependent to subject-independent. HT precision stays pinned near 0.50 for every model — a property of the features, not the estimator.

F11.title: ROC curves (headline tabular models)
F11.caption: ROC for XGBoost, XGBoost-tuned and TabPFN, recomputed from held-out test probabilities. AUC drops markedly from the dependent to the independent split, quantifying the leakage in the optimistic regime.

F12.title: Precision–Recall curves (HT class)
F12.caption: Precision–recall for the HT (ASD-model) minority class. The dashed line is HT prevalence (no-skill). Precision degrades sharply at high recall on the independent split.

F13.title: Confusion matrices (headline models)
F13.caption: Test-set confusion matrices at threshold 0.5. The dominant error in every panel is WT recordings predicted HT (false positives), consistent with the ~0.50 HT-precision ceiling.

F14.title: Feature importance (XGBoost)
F14.caption: Top-15 features by XGBoost gain importance, averaged across the dependent and independent models. Per-syllable-type start/end frequencies and durations dominate — consistent with Shekel et al. (2021); note the syllN columns map type N→slot via a documented off-by-one.

F15.title: Per-strain comparison
F15.caption: XGBoost per-strain results. strain1 (recent mixed-background cohort) is highly separable even leak-free (acc 0.90), whereas strain2 (small pure-BALB/c cohort) collapses on the minority class under the independent split — evidence that strain/cohort confounds genotype.

F16.title: HT-precision wall
F16.caption: HT precision at the default threshold across every tabular configuration clusters near 0.50 (only the easier strain1 cohort escapes). About half of all positive calls are false alarms — a ceiling set by the features.

F17.title: Threshold-objective operating points
F17.caption: Effect of the threshold objective on TabPFN. On the dependent split, f1/target_recall lift HT precision to ~0.62 while holding recall ~0.81; on the independent split, Youden/balanced degenerate (recall→1, precision pinned ~0.48), so target_recall is the only sensible objective.

F18.title: Sequence-model lever sweep and CV deflation
F18.caption: Left: balanced accuracy across the A–H imbalance-handling levers (E run only for BiLSTM). Right: the lucky single-split BiLSTM independent score (0.704) deflates to 0.563 ± 0.063 under 5-fold grouped CV — the honest sequence-model signal is weak and data-limited.

F19.title: Annotated segmentation example
F19.caption: Spectrogram of a representative pup recording with the 35 automatically detected syllables overlaid (blue boxes span each call's time extent and start/end-frequency band). Source: USV_Recordings/2015/08009N_HT/08139-2L_HT/day_6/session2/T0000019.WAV.
